facts.statement: The genus Cladornis was described by Ameghino in 1895.
Cladornis lived in Argentina during the early Oligocene.
facts.quote: Cladornis is an extinct genus of bird from the early Oligocene of Argentina.

facts.statement: The genus is known from a single partial tarsometatarsus fossil.
facts.quote: Known from a single partial tarsometatarsus

facts.statement: The taxonomic placement of Cladornis is uncertain.
The shaft of the Cladornis tarsometatarsus was very flat and short.
facts.quote: The shaft of the tarsometatarsus of Cladornis was very flat and short

facts.statement: The distal head of the Cladornis tarsometatarsus suggests strong development of the toes.
facts.quote: the distal head suggests strong development of the toes.

facts.statement: Cladornis belongs to the parent group Cladornithidae.
Cladornis is classified in the family Cladornithidae.
Cladornis lived between 33.9 and 23.04 million years ago, from the Rupelian to the Chattian stages.
facts.quote: Time range: Rupelian to Chattian (33.9 to 23.04 million years ago)

rejected.statement: Researchers have debated whether Cladornis was a terrestrial penguin, a pelecaniform, or a very large and extremely weird land bird.
rejected.quote: It has been variously described as some kind of terrestrial penguin, a pelecaniform, and a 'very large and extremely weird land bird'.
rejected.reason: quote not found verbatim in the source

rejected.statement: Cladornis is a member of the class Aves.
